name: Reflection Hall
description: A walk-in 5x5x3 m chamber of six reflective walls. Step through the small entrance, grab a glowing ball from the rack (or fire the console launcher), and throw it. Every wall bounce computes the law of reflection r = d - 2(d.n̂)n̂ off that surface's inward normal and blooms an annotation cluster AT the impact point: the incident throw d (orange), the wall normal n̂ (cyan), and the reflected ray r (magenta), plus the live formula with real numbers and a check that r matches the ball's new velocity. Each ball carries a velocity arrow and trails a fading ribbon of its path. The room is built at true metre scale — no shrink — so reflection is a thing you stand inside.
theoreticalGrounding: The law of reflection r = d - 2(d.n̂)n̂. A mirror keeps the component of the incoming vector tangent to the wall and flips only the component along the normal. Speed is conserved; reflection is conservation with a sign change. The dot product d.n̂ is the slice that points into the wall — double it, subtract it twice along n̂, and you have the bounce.

reflection_hall.name: Reflection Hall
reflection_hall.description: Six StaticBody3D walls (floor, ceiling, +X, -X, +Z) enclose a 5x5x3 m room; the -Z wall is two side panels + a lintel leaving a 1.2x2.2 m entrance you walk through. An invisible doorway curtain on the ball-only collision layer keeps thrown balls inside while letting the player pass. Balls are RigidBody3D with a bouncy physics material (engine bounces; we visualise). Each ball caches its pre-contact velocity every physics frame; on wall contact it recovers the incident d, looks up the wall's inward normal n̂, computes r = d - 2(d.n̂)n̂, and spawns a ~1.5 s fading d/n̂/r arrow cluster + live formula at the hit point, verifying r against the post-bounce velocity. Fading per-ball trails via ImmediateMesh line strips. A grab-throw ball rack (primary VR) plus an optional ANGLE/FORCE/FIRE console; on desktop/headless the console auto-fires every ~3 s so captures show live bounces. DNA: ball_bounce, gravity_scale, launch_speed, room dimensions.
reflection_hall.qfep_connection: F_force: a bounce is a deterministic reflection of velocity about a wall's normal — speed conserved, one component's sign flipped. The room performs r = d - 2(d.n̂)n̂ for you, six walls' worth, until the throw becomes felt law.
